UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for *Ralstonia solanacearum* prhI, an ECF sigma factor you need for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node. Its dorsum slopes down posteriorly, so the posterior face is short. Now the head. The dorsum is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here's what we found about foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a was highly restricted in the male. foxl2b, the diverged paralog, showed up in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b was highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, though, foxl2b expression was very strong. That matches earlier findings showing foxl2b present and foxl2a absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Put together, these results suggest foxl2b may regulate male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot substantiate carbon neutrality claims for electrical use beyond a claimant's metered consumption, because most RECs come from projects that were financially viable without their sale. [10] Consequently, they lack additionality. Additionality is a counterfactual test: it asks what would have happened under the status quo if the REC had not been purchased or contracted. Many additionality testing frameworks exist, but the core question is the same in each one: did the project's financial survival depend on REC revenues? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

We start from the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975) and derive a time-dependent mild-slope equation. From it we get the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion for steady waves, we recover equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows what matters: the modified curvature terms of the MMSE are significant, while the slope square terms stay negligible under the mild-slope assumption. So we keep every modified curvature term the MSE drops. That gives us a uniform model.

To predict wave scattering by a varying bottom, we built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM). The uniform model captures the main features of waves over various sea beds, sinusoidal beds and man-made bars included. On sinusoidal beds, it matches experimental data more closely than other established models. On man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model match the data more closely than Kirby (1986).

The FEM model also applies to the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

It deals with a former existence instead of a future one, and portrays a conflict between reason, supported by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts within us. In this account, the human soul has traveled in the company of some god and perceived truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the result of a struggle that took place earlier. This world is a relative construct, often projected into a future, much as we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it is as influential and widespread as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech, and the majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can only be rendered inadequately in another language.

MapleStory has thousands of monsters. Here's where they live and how to survive them.

The weak monsters are the most common, and they live near towns. They wander aimlessly even if you bump into them, so you can just take the damage they deal.

The aggro mechanic: monsters usually roam aimlessly even if you bump into them, but if you attack an enemy or cast a debuff on it, you "aggro" it. That means it notices you and tries to attack you back.

Here's something worth knowing about early hearing development. Children typically develop spoken language in their first few years. A hearing impairment can block both: the ability to speak, and the ability to understand speech.

Often, nobody notices a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child's deficit right away. By the time it's apparent, communication problems may have already strained the family and held back the child's social skills. A child raised in a Deaf community, where people sign instead of speak, can avoid those problems (see our article on Deaf Culture).

That's why many developed countries test newborns' hearing, so a deaf child doesn't grow up isolated in a hearing family without anyone realizing. Sign language is a full means of communication, but literacy still depends on understanding speech. In most written languages, the sound of a word is coded in symbols.

Someone who heard well enough to learn to speak and read keeps that ability even if their hearing later fades to the point of not hearing voices. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely reads proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence points the same way: identify hearing impairment early, and a child with very insensitive hearing has the best chance of learning spoken language. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

Transduction is what happens when a physical or chemical signal becomes a neural impulse. In the nervous system, it's the process that turns stimuli into electrical signals. Sensory receptors do the converting: they take a physical or chemical input and turn it into an electrical impulse that travels to the brain.

Look at your visual system. In the retina, rod and cone cells form the bridge between the physical world and neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, the protein rhodopsin changes shape. That molecular shift sets off a cascade of events that alters the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. As the gradient drops, so do the electrical signals sent to the brain. The result: more light hitting the photoreceptor means fewer electrical impulses. That inversion is how your brain decodes the visual world with such precision.

Subject: Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area: What You Need to Know

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), or just the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It's made up of former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

Roughly five million people live here. That's considerably more than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. Motorways crisscross the region, yet hitchhiking is hard work, because the minor roads form a complicated network. The main routes are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you're hitching here, stick to those motorways. The smaller roads carry almost no transit traffic, which makes them nearly useless. Germany is generally a pleasant country to hitch through, but the Ruhr Area is its most unpleasant stretch by far. Think of Istanbul: the cities here are independent, yet to a traveler they blur into one massive city.

Good luck planning your trip.

Best regards,

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Here are the key findings from our lung tissue volume and aeration analysis.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, for any compartment with a CT number above zero.

To get the change in functional residual capacity from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC), we took the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between the PEEP and ZEEP states. We defined alveolar derecruitment the same way, but only for gas volume in poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions.

We also measured how gas volume changed with PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated regions, those with CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

For each patient, we classified the distribution of lost aeration (lung morphology) as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on CT attenuations at ZEEP, following reference [21].

Mobile internet is changing how stories can pull you in, because electronic games now run on portable, location-aware interfaces. These games are the latest stage in a decades-long evolution: games that want you to be a co-author alongside the original designers, not just an avatar in someone else's gameworld.

Location-aware interfaces let you fold places in the physical world into your gameworld, and the other way around. No earlier interactive media could do that. Mobile games also abandon linear narratives. Their cooperative storytelling is built on your experience of place.

The "author-player" worldmaking idea existed before mobile games, but mobile games push the process further than traditional video games allow. The worldmaking extends past the screen into the physical world, so the interfaces use your sensory experiences of real places as storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and describe what happened when we tried to use that potential while designing and implementing our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.
